implementation_boundary.rule: The Clark TUI is original Clark code. It shares Clark domain and provider contracts with Desktop and does not load, invoke, vendor, or test against another TUI implementation.

features.title: Clark authentication, organization resolution, workspace selection, and initialization
behaviors: Interactive startup offers browser, device-code, and API-key authentication without requiring Clark Desktop
The Clark credential resolves account, organization choices, project, plan, and specialist entitlements server-side
Code and all four paid specialists are workspace choices rather than slash commands

features.title: Deliberately small Clark-owned human terminal surface
behaviors: The public palette contains exactly eight Clark commands
Unknown imported commands fail locally instead of becoming model prompts
The renderer has no Vim mode, themes, pets, background-terminal console, review console, or side-chat command surface

features.title: Shared Provider contract, typed events, streaming, steering, and transcript rendering
behaviors: The TUI consumes agent_core Provider events without a terminal-specific provider protocol
Streaming, structured specialist output, artifacts, goals, usage, errors, cancel, and steering remain typed
The composer supports multiline human input, paste, history, selection, and bounded terminal layout

features.title: Fail-closed provider permissions and persistent Clark profiles
behaviors: Provider-authored choices, risks, reasons, and consequences remain visible
Missing choices fail closed and persistent profiles never silently widen the current session

features.title: One structured attachment command for files and editor context
behaviors: Exact and fuzzy files retain filename, MIME type, and byte-exact payloads
Editor context uses /attach --ide and multi-file context is staged atomically
Unsupported media fails before a provider turn starts

features.title: Provider-owned model choice, durable goal state, and sourced status
behaviors: Model choices come from the active Clark provider and specialist-owned models stay locked
Durable goal state is typed provider state rather than transcript inference
Status attributes authentication, organization, plan, workspace, provider, sync, configuration, and usage to their source

features.title: Distinct Scientist, RSI, Scout, and Security workflows
behaviors: Each paid specialist has its own workspace modes and typed provider outputs
Specialist selection is entitlement-gated before a worker or model starts
The common TUI renders specialist events without flattening specialists into generic commands

features.title: Mandatory cloud continuity for every paid specialist
behaviors: Scientist journals, experiments, evidence, and artifacts require verified Clark Cloud receipts
RSI research and world artifacts, Scout workspace state, and Security scan state use their authoritative cloud paths
Headless work fails loudly before execution when authentication, entitlement, preflight synchronization, or required completion synchronization fails

probes.contains: No worker or model was started
No worker or model was started

features.title: One account-scoped conversation service shared by GUI, TUI, and headless Clark
behaviors: Desktop, TUI, and headless Clark reopen the same cloud-backed conversation and specialist state
The shared service owns account isolation, provider binding, resume transcripts, and sync receipts
The TUI does not introduce a separate local JSON session database

features.title: Standalone Clark CLI installation and update
behaviors: The clark executable contains the human TUI and does not require Clark Desktop
Checksum-verified CLI and headless artifacts are released for supported platforms
